items.body: Carolina captain tore calf Oct. 11, plans to accompany team to Finland MORRISVILLE, N.C. -- Jordan Staal was back on the ice with the Carolina Hurricanes on Saturday and hopes to return during the 2026 NHL Global Series Finland next week. The Hurricanes center and captain is recovering from a torn calf muscle sustained during warmups prior to a 4-1 win at the Philadelphia Flyers on Oct. 11. Carolina (13-3-2) hosts the Chicago Blackhawks on Saturday (8 p.m. ET HHN, CARNHL, CHSN) in their final game before leaving for Helsinki, where it will face the Seattle Kraken on Nov. 12 and 14. Staal fully intends to be on the cross-Atlantic flight and practice with the Hurricanes on Monday and Tuesday. “I haven't really practiced the team,” he said Saturday. “I'd like to get a couple in and see how I feel. Flying across the ocean and not playing in games wouldn't be the smartest thing, so I'd like to try to play, but we'll see how it goes.” Carolina would also have a morning skate next Thursday, a practice on Friday and a morning skate Saturday to potentially give Staal more work to play in the second game against Seattle. “I would like to try,” he said. “I can't say I promise that. I mean, if I'm going to fly all the way over there, I’d like to play in a game, if everything goes smooth. If it doesn't, then it doesn't, but that's fine.” Staal won the Conn Smythe Trophy last season as the most valuable player of the Stanley Cup Playoffs (12 points; eight goals, four assists in 19 games) after leading Carolina to its first championship since 2006. items.body: Lightning forward joined by family at special ceremony at University of Nebraska Omaha Tampa Bay Lightning forward Jake Guentzel returned to his roots on Friday, celebrating his jersey retirement and induction into the Omaha Athletics Hall of Fame at the University of Nebraska Omaha. Guentzel – one of the most successful hockey players in Omaha’s history – went back to Kemp Ice for the Hall of Fame ceremony and became the first Omaha Hockey player to have his jersey lifted into the rafters. His wife, Natalie Johnson (who also went to Omaha), and their two young kids joined Guentzel at the event. A special moment for the entire Guentzel family! ❤️ #OMAHockey pic.twitter.com/dAnGoQUN0d Guentzel was born in Omaha and played three seasons at the university from 2013 until 2016. He led the team to an NCAA Frozen Four appearance in 2015, before embarking on his professional hockey journey which has now included a Stanley Cup and an Olympic gold medal. He finished his career at Omaha with 40 goals and 79 assists in 108 games.

items.summary: The Bruins have called up Mike Eyssimont from their AHL affiliate, the Providence Bruins.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images Some roster moves in Beantown, with a young player staying on the shelf for a little bit. On Saturday, the Boston Bruins announced that forward James Hagens has been placed on injured reserve. In response, the team called up forward Mikey Eyssimont from their American Hockey League affiliate, the Providence Bruins. Hagens is listed out with an undisclosed injury, with his placement on IR retroactive to Nov. 5. That night, the Bruins took on the Pittsburgh Penguins . In the second period, Hagens received a cross-check to his side from Penguins defenseman Samuel Girard. Hagens went down the tunnel to the Boston locker room, but did not return. The Bruins went on to win the contest, 5-2. Per the league’s IR rules, Hagens could return as early as next Saturday, when the Bruins host the Minnesota Wild. However, the team is considering the former Boston College star to be week-to-week. For the B’s, seeing Hagens out of action puts a damper on what has been an impressive start to his rookie season. Through 17 games, the 20-year-old has scored six goals and six assists for 12 points, sitting tied for second on the team in goals and tied for fifth in overall scoring. His efforts have helped put Boston up with the top teams in the Atlantic Division through one month of the 2026-27 campaign. Despite playing 56 games with the Bruins last year, Eyssimont has started this season in the AHL, but has been productive. In eight games with Providence, the 30-year-old has notched 13 goals and 16 points, both team highs through the first month of the year. items.title: Did Oilers' McDavid Overreact To Helleson And Ducks Incident?
items.summary: Edmonton Oilers captain Connor McDavid wasn't too pleased about the hit he took into the net from Anaheim Ducks defenseman Drew Helleson. But is McDavid's response a bit of an overreaction?
items.body: Perry Nelson-Imagn Images Perry Nelson-Imagn Images Did Oilers' McDavid Overreact To Helleson And Ducks Incident? Adam Proteau Partner Nov 7, 2026 6:00 PM Published Nov 7, 2026 6:00 PM Edmonton Oilers captain Connor McDavid wasn't too pleased about the hit he took into the net from Anaheim Ducks defenseman Drew Helleson. But is McDavid's response a bit of an overreaction? For the most part, in his Hockey Hall of Fame-level career, Edmonton Oilers superstar center Connor McDavid has been a cool, calm, unflappable icon. So it’s rare to see him get angry – at least, not outside of the Oilers’ dressing room. So it was a little out of character to see McDavid going off on Anaheim Ducks defenseman Drew Helleson after he drove McDavid into the Ducks’ net. McDavid stayed down on the ice briefly, and when he got up, it was clear that he was upset with Helleson. And his post-game comments confirmed it. More Videos “Obviously, it’s a play that is a little sensitive to me,” McDavid said after Thursday's game . “Those are plays that I’ve been really, really hurt on before. Going into the end wall, going into the net…Those type of plays I find to be dangerous. Obviously, I didn’t love it.” Now, we’ve seen plenty of hyper-aggressive players target the opposition with over-the-top acts that seriously injure an NHLer. But this wasn’t a particularly egregious act on Helleson’s part, looking back at the footage. McDavid's feelings on the matter are respected, but this case could’ve been an overreaction. items.title: Leafs’ Tavares to return after nine-game absence
items.summary: Tavares has been sidelined with a lower-body injury since last month, but returns on Saturday to face Montreal.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Nick Turchiaro-Imagn Images Some promising news for a Toronto Maple Leafs team that needs a jolt. When speaking to the media, Maple Leafs head coach Jim Hiller announced that forward John Tavares will be in the lineup on Saturday night, when the team plays host to the Montreal Canadiens. Tavares has missed the last nine games due to a lower-body injury that knocked him out of a game against the Buffalo Sabres on Oct. 15. During that time, Toronto went on a four-game win streak, but has slipped over the past week, going 5-4-0 during the former captain’s absence. The Toronto native had been showing signs that he could come back soon, as he was taking reps on the Leafs’ top power-play unit during practice on Friday. One thing that will be different is that Tavares won’t be in his normal position. As he’s been closing in on a full bill of health, No. 91 started taking reps on the wing, playing on the left side of Toronto’s second line, centered by Nick Paul with William Nylander on the right wing. Prior to his injury, Tavares had been one of the team’s consistent scorers through the opening weeks of the 2026-27 campaign. In seven appearances, the 36-year-old has scored two goals and five assists for seven points, with a plus/minus of -5 while averaging 16:31 of ice time. Tavares entered the new campaign looking to make the most of his time with his hometown team, after rumors swirled that he might not return to the Leafs, even after he posted back-to-back 30-goal seasons. Yet, the team re-signed the former London Knight to a four-year contract in June, with the deal carrying an AAV of $4.38 million . The Leafs (8-7-2) sit seventh in the Atlantic Division, two points back of a Wild Card spot in the Eastern Conference.

items.title: Quick Shifts: Vinni Lettieri is fighting to survive in the NHL
items.summary: With the Maple Leafs returning to health, Vinni Lettieri is literally fighting to keep his spot in the lineup. Whatever it takes. Luke Fox digs into his battle and 11 more observations from around in the NHL in this edition of Quick Shifts.
items.body: A quick mix of the things we gleaned from the week of hockey, serious and less so, and rolling four lines deep. I don’t need to crash into you to drink your wine. 1. In the NHL, one man’s return to health always spells bad news for one of his teammates. And so, while the Toronto Maple Leafs get a nice boost with John Tavares jumping into their lineup this weekend, Vinni Lettieri quietly slides to the outside. The 31-year-old journeyman is literally fighting to stick in the show. Lettieri is undrafted, he’s five-foot-10, and he’s changed teams five times, never making more than six figures. Last season, he never got called up. Spent the whole winter on the farm. So, when the Minnesota native got off to a hot start with the Marlies and was promoted to the Leafs in the wake of injuries, he dropped the mitts twice in four days, taking on Connor Murphy in Edmonton and Cale Fleury in Seattle. “My last NHL fight was Scott Laugton in pre-season when I was with the New York Rangers nine years ago,” Lettieri says. “With those two fights, I've had three in my whole career.” Lettieri scored once in his eight-game look and outlasted Bo Groulx, who was waived down. But with Dakota Joshua and Tavares back in action and Kirill Marchenko on the mend, the bottom-six skater is desperate to find a way onto the scoresheet and into the coach’s good books. “I just feel like I've been stuck for a long time. items.summary: The Toronto Maple Leafs have activated forward John Tavares off IR and recalled goaltender Artur Akhtyamov from AHL Toronto.
items.body: Register Login Maple Leafs Activate John Tavares, Recall Artur Akhtyamov By Brian La Rose | at November 7, 2026 11:26 am The Maple Leafs have made a pair of roster moves in advance of their game tonight against Montreal. Per the NHL’s media site, Toronto has activated forward John Tavares off injured reserve and recalled goaltender Artur Akhtyamov from AHL Toronto. The activation of Tavares should come as no surprise after he was a full participant in practice on Friday. The 36-year-old has missed the last nine games with a lower-body injury, stalling what had been another strong start to his season. Before being sidelined, Tavares had two goals and five assists in his first seven appearances. Tavares should slot back in on Toronto’s second line, though it remains to be seen if he’ll go back down the middle or line up on the wing in the short term. A natural middleman, there has been talk of trying to shift him to the wing at times, which would allow Nick Paul to stay down the middle on the second line. He’ll likely take the place of either Vinni Lettieri or Zack MacEwen in their lineup against Montreal, giving a boost to a Maple Leafs offensive group that is already among the best in the league. Meanwhile, this is Akhtyamov’s second recall of the early season. He received a brief recall last month to serve as the backup for a couple of games, allowing both Sergei Bobrovsky and Anthony Stolarz to have a full game of rest. Lundell has four goals and two assists for six points, averaging 17:41 of ice time in 16 games with the Panthers in 2026-27. He’s in the third season of a six-year, $30-million contract signed ahead of the 2024-25 campaign. Now in his sixth NHL season, the Finnish center has 82 goals and 125 assists for 207 points in 375 career regular-season games. He also has 12 goals and 34 assists for 46 points in 77 career playoff games, and was a major contributor during Florida’s back-to-back Stanley Cup championships in 2024 and 2025. Taken No. 12 overall in the 2020 NHL Entry Draft, Lundell spent three seasons with HIFK Helsinki in the top Finnish men’s league, where he would score 35 goals and 37 assists for 72 points in 108 regular-season games. items.body: The IIHF has come to a decision regarding Russian and Belarusian participation in upcoming tournaments. Following a ruling last week from the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) to reinstate Russia to international hockey competitions, the IIHF stated on Saturday that, while it disagrees with the ruling, it is taking the steps required by the CAS's decision regarding possible reimplementation. "While the IIHF continues to disagree with the decision of the Court of Arbitration for Sport concerning Russian participation in IIHF Championships, we are taking the necessary steps required by the CAS ruling and reviewing what conditions would need to be met to safeguard our Championships, protect the organization's financial stability and secure the long-term future of international ice hockey," the IIHF said in its statement. "The IIHF must work within the applicable framework while upholding its responsibility to preserve international competition and protect the sport as a whole. "The IIHF is therefore exploring all available avenues, including opening discussions with all affected MNAs (Member National Associations), including the Russian Ice Hockey Federation, to identify a constructive way forward that serves the interests of global ice hockey." Last week on Friday, the CAS overturned an exclusion of Russian participation in international ice hockey tournaments, put in place since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. The IIHF has opposed Russia's immediate reinstatement, citing security, logistical and competitive concerns, while several European hockey federations have said their teams would refuse to face Russia. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Minnesota Wild made history Friday night, becoming the fastest team in NHL history to reach 1,000 regular-seaon wins as they defeated the San Jose Sharks 4-1. Minnesota was led by Kirill Kaprizov on Friday, who scored his league-leading 16th goal and added three assists. The forward has five goals and eight assists for 13 points during a seven-game point streak. Defenseman Quinn Hughes had a goal and two assists in the win. The Wild accomplished the feat in 1,995 games played, which beat the previous mark held by the Philadelphia Flyers who did it in 2,018 games. In January 2025 , the Nashville Predators did it in 2,020 games. The Wild are now 12-3-3 and possess the best record in the Western Conference and the second-best mark in the NHL . Meanwhile, the Sharks are 7-10-1 through their first 18 games of 2026-27. Minnesota entered the league as an expansion franchise in 2000-01. They reached the Western Conference Final in just their third season, but have not reached since. Mikko Koivu, who served as captain for 11 seasons, holds multiple franchise records, including the most regular-season games played (1,028) assists (504) and points (709). Meanwhile, Kaprizov is the Wild’s all-time franchise leader with 246 goals. Now in his seventh NHL season, he has 259 assists and 505 points in 415 career games.

items.summary: As delighted as Johnny Bower was to be inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame a half-century ago this year, the Toronto Maple Leafs legend was probably even happier for the goalies who were enshrined before and after him.
items.body: Legendary goalie, enshrined 50 years ago, won Cup with Maple Leafs four times As delighted as Johnny Bower was to be inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame a half-century ago this year, the Toronto Maple Leafs legend was probably even happier for the goalies who were enshrined before and after him. There was something that Bower especially enjoyed about his pads-wearing lodge brothers being joined together in this celebrated fraternity after they’d faced the final shot of their careers. Bower was the 25th of 44 goalies to be inducted into the Hall of Fame, a number that soon will grow to 46 with the inductions on Monday of Carey Price and Pekka Rinne, respectively of the Montreal Canadiens and Nashville Predators. Johnny Bower awaits a shot during a game at Toronto’s Maple Leaf Gardens. Bower died of pneumonia at age 93 on Dec. 26, 2017, having been a hugely popular presence on the red carpet at Brookfield Place for many years. Unfailingly humble, he was almost embarrassed when he was stopped for a photo or a chat on his way into the induction ceremony, and so modest was he that he sometimes needed to be talked into attending the gala event. Bower was elected to the shrine 50 years ago as a member of the Class of 1976, inducted with rugged defenseman Bill Quackenbush and members of the Builder category Jack Gibson, Philip Ross and William Wirtz. “This is really wonderful,” he said upon being elected. “It’s a great honor. It’s nice to know your name will be on the honor roll. I didn’t expect to get in this soon (six years after his final game).” Boston Bruins defenseman Bill Quackenbush, here in 1955, and Toronto Maple Leafs goalie Johnny Bower, in 1965, were the two players inducted in the Hockey Hall of Fame’s Class of 1976. items.body: Register Login Mammoth Recall Gregor Biber, Place Kailer Yamamoto On IR By Brian La Rose | at November 6, 2026 9:00 pm With Nate Schmidt suffering an upper-body injury on Thursday in Montreal, the Mammoth have made a pair of roster moves to get another blueliner on their active roster. Biber was a fourth-round pick by Utah in 2024, going 98th overall. He becomes the first player from their draft class that year to receive an NHL recall. The Austria native made the move to play in Sweden in his draft year, playing in Rogle’s junior system. He then moved up to the SHL level, getting into 88 games over the last two seasons, recording just three goals and two assists in the two campaigns combined. Still, the Mammoth liked enough of what they saw to sign Biber to a three-year, entry-level contract back in May. The 20-year-old has had a decent start to his playing career in North America, notching three assists and 10 penalty minutes in his first 11 games with the Roadrunners. He will likely serve as the seventh defender behind Artem Duda until Schmidt is able to return. As for Yamamoto, he is dealing with an upper-body injury that has cost him a little more than a week so far despite the original day-to-day designation. items.title: ‘Remarkable’: Gretzky gives McDavid flowers amid historically hot start
items.summary: Despite seeing his records at risk, Gretzky had nothing but praise for the current Oilers superstar as he pushes to break The Great One’s single-season points record.
items.body: Not long ago, the prospect of any of Wayne Gretzky's records being broken felt far-fetched. Fast forward to today, and Alexander Ovechkin has taken the top spot in the all-time goal tally, and Connor McDavid may be on pace to erase another Gretzky high point. Despite seeing his records at risk, Gretzky had nothing but praise for the current Oilers superstar as he pushes to break The Great One 's single-season points record. “Remarkable,” Gretzky said at a ceremony on Friday at the Hockey Hall of Fame. “What he’s doing for his hockey team, and for the game, and for the city of Edmonton, it’s unmatched right now. I think he’s on a mission to win a Stanley Cup. He wants it desperately, and that’s what you need out of your best player and out of your captain." “You need that leadership that, you want to get to the next level, and he has that.” McDavid has been on a historic tear to start the season, picking up 44 points in 17 games, and is on pace to reach 217 — a mark that would top Gretzky’s record of 215 points set in 1985-86. The 29-year-old has had some stellar point tallies over the course of his 12-year career, including a 153-point benchmark (with a league-leading 64 goals and 89 assists) in the 2022-23 season, but breaking the 200-point threshold has still been a ways away — as it has for every player not named Gretzky Gretzky is the only NHL player to ever reach 200 points in a season, passing the plateau four times over his 20-year career.

items.summary: The Hammers also signed former Dallas Stars prospect Antonio Stranges to a PTO.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Isaiah J. Downing-Imagn Images A former NHL star is trying to stay in the game. On Friday, the Hamilton Hammers, the American Hockey League affiliate of the New York Islanders , announced that the team has signed forward Robby Fabbri to a professional tryout. Fabbri started the 2026-27 season without a contract, after a season in which he saw limited playing time. After starting the 2025-26 campaign on a PTO with the AHL’s Charlotte Checkers, the Mississauga, Ont. native signed a one-year contract with the St. Louis Blues in December. He dressed in 15 games for the Blues, scoring four points, before being put on waivers. He was claimed by the Minnesota Wild , scoring a goal in six games. He didn’t dress for any of Minnesota’s games in the Stanley Cup Playoffs. In 21 regular-season games last year, Fabbri posted two goals and three assists for five points. Fabbri has appeared in 463 regular-season games in his NHL career, scoring 108 goals and 113 assists for 221 points. The 30-year-old also has 16 points in 30 playoff games, including a Stanley Cup with the Blues in 2019. Fabbri also has eight points in 12 AHL games. The Hammers also signed forward Antonio Stranges to a PTO. The former London Knight was a fourth-round pick by the Dallas Stars in 2020, but has yet to make it to the NHL. He has scored 47 goals and 113 points in 208 regular-season games with the Stars’ top farm team, the Texas Stars, with another five points in 18 Calder Cup Playoff games. The Hammers (3-8-0-2) are struggling since relocating from Bridgeport. The team sits last in the North Division, despite playing more games than the rest of their division. Hamilton is set to host the Providence Bruins on Friday night.

O’Connor is in his second full season with the team, and at 28 years of age, he isn’t likely to be a central piece during the next era of winning hockey in Vancouver. O’Connor isn’t the biggest or most skilled player, but he has a decent mix of speed, size, experience, and versatility, including the ability to play in the bottom six, which should make him an attractive piece for a contending team looking to add depth to its third or fourth line. From a Canucks perspective, they have every reason to move O’Connor and other veterans who didn’t figure into their future. The Canucks have embarked on what could be a long rebuild and need to grab as many future assets as possible to turn things around quickly. There have been whispers that Vancouver is hoping to move veterans, and O’Connor might be the easiest player to move given his utility and the low cost to acquire him. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources One of the more (positively) surprising starts to the NHL season belongs to the Seattle Kraken . At 19 points through 15 games, the Kraken’s above-average start has them sitting in the Pacific Division’s third seed a little more than a month into the season. In arguably the NHL’s weakest division, the next closest team behind the Kraken are the Anaheim Ducks , who are two points behind having played one additional game. Kraken GM Jason Botterill made a hard push for Dallas Stars winger Jason Robertson this summer, reportedly offering the then-RFA an eight-year contract with an AAV in the neighborhood of $15 million. According to Kraken sources, the team is still looking to add, and as one source said, they are “big-game hunting.” Given the overall weakness of the Pacific Division, striking while the iron is hot would behoove Botterill. The Kraken have been in what one could call the “mushy middle” for the lion’s share of their existence since 2021. They have made the playoffs just once in that span, earning a first-round win versus the then-reigning Stanley Cup champion Colorado Avalanche . The Kraken have since been too good to pick any higher than seventh in the draft, keeping them just outside the playoff picture and without the ability to draft a true, can’t-miss superstar while also not offering enough playing time for their younger players. Despite his high-end skill and skating qualities, Nylander can be one of the most frustrating star-caliber players when it comes to the defensive side of the game. items.body: It's taken longer than expected for Ivan Demidov to return from injury, but signs are pointing in the right direction. Demidov, who has been out since Oct. 3 with a lower-body injury, has been skating with the Montreal Canadiens and is progressing in his recovery, but does not have an exact timeline for his return, general manager Kent Hughes told Sportsnet's Eric Engels on Thursday. Though Demidov was originally given a recovery timeline of two to four weeks, more than a month has passed since he took the ice for the Canadiens in game action. However, Hughes said that Demidov hasn't suffered any setbacks, adding that timelines are approximate — particularly as it concerns Demidov's injury. It's unclear how exactly Demidov suffered the injury, but the 20-year-old had played in the Canadiens' first two games of the season against the Maple Leafs and Penguins. He missed practice following the game against Pittsburgh and was placed on injured reserve soon after. Demidov finished second in Calder Trophy voting last season, recording 62 points (19 goals, 43 assists) in 82 games while skating 15:30 of ice time per night. He had one goal and one assist in his two games this year before injury. Detroit, according to Pierre LeBrun , wants Larkin’s camp to expand his trade list, as they are having difficulty getting a trade to work. “Here’s where I’d say the situation is at right now – it’s a bit of a game of poker in that the Red Wings have told Larkin’s camp they feel like they’ve exhausted every option here with these 10 teams on his list,” said LeBrun on Insider Trading. “They’re just not there with a trade that makes sense for them. items.title: German government wants to keep hockey worlds as Russia’s return leads to boycott
items.body: BERLIN — Germany's government wants to keep the men's ice hockey world championships in the country “as planned” after the reinstatement of Russia by a sports court last week caused nearly half of the 16 teams to threaten a boycott. The German hockey federation has suggested it could give up hosting rights for the event in Duesseldorf and Mannheim in May rather than deal with uncertainty over extra security and higher costs. Seven European nations' hockey federations including those in Finland and Sweden — though not Germany — have said they will compete in the championships but will boycott games against Russia. “It needs to be our aim to hold the tournaments as planned,” government spokesperson Stefan Kornelius said Friday. “That would, however, not in fact be possible given the boycotts if Russia is to participate. Therefore we now want to explore options through discussions to enable us to still have the tournament take place.” Russia had been excluded from International Ice Hockey Federation events since its invasion of Ukraine in 2022, until a Court of Arbitration for Sport ruling last week compelled the IIHF to let Russia back in. Besides the boycott plans, the IIHF has come under pressure from major sponsors threatening to end their agreements or refuse to have their logos displayed if Russia plays. Russia has said it expects to be awarded wins by forfeit if other countries refuse to play. The Russian Foreign Ministry has also criticized the Canadian government's plans to exclude Russia from the world junior championships there starting next month. The women’s world championship starting in Denmark on Friday is not affected by the CAS ruling and is going ahead without Russia.

items.body: DENVER — Steven Stamkos scored a power-play goal 2:18 into overtime, Justus Annunen made 30 saves and the Nashville Predators beat the Colorado Avalanche 3-2 on Thursday night. It was Stamkos' 247th goal on the power play, tying him with Luc Robitaille for fifth-most in NHL history. Stamkos also drew the penalty, too.. Ross Colton scored against his former team, and Vitali Pinchuk had his first career goal as the Predators moved to 2-0 over Colorado this season. Jaden Schwartz and Parker Kelly had goals for the Avalanche, who are 6-1-2 at home this season. Mackenzie Blackwood stopped 22 of 25 shots. He got some help, too, with Nazem Kadri knocking away a puck that was trickling toward the net. The Predators weathered a holding penalty on Steven Stamkos with 3:07 left in regulation. They had a 2-on-1 chance, too, but couldn’t convert. Nashville and Colorado both struggled on the power play as the Predators finished 1 for 5 and the Avalanche went 0 for 3. The Predators had 25 blocked shots. Pinchuk gave the Predators a 2-1 lead in the opening period with a slick backhanded shot that went over the shoulder of Blackwood. The 24-year-old Pinchuk nearly had a goal earlier in the period but his shot clanged off the post. A video was shown on the big screen to honor Colton and Jack Drury, who were both traded from Colorado to the Predators in June. The clip aired shortly after Colton's fourth goal of the season. items.title: Oilers’ McDavid passionate in response to ‘dangerous’ hit
items.summary: This incident runs a little deeper for McDavid. And he was passionate in his post-game remarks.
items.body: EDMONTON — They may call him McJesus, but Connor McDavid doesn’t expect the seas to part every time he wants to take the puck to the net. “I’m not expecting him to give me a free pass. He makes his decision, I make my decision, that’s just the way it is,” said McDavid after being driven into the goalpost by Anaheim defenceman Drew Helleson early in a thrilling 5-4 Ducks win. “You’re going to hit me like that and there’s going to be a response, that’s just the way it is.” In-game, Vasily Podkolzin did what nearly every Canadian hockey fan deems appropriate when an opponent risks injury to your captain, the best player on your team — and in this case, the best player in the world. Podkolzin beat the wheels off Helleson, coupling a bevy of rights with a passel of lefts. Given little choice but to defend himself, Helleson opted out. Podkolzin politely declined to accept that decision, and was given an instigator and a game misconduct for his efforts. “The instigation of the whole thing was when they run our guy into the net,” spat head coach Mike Babcock. “Is it within the rules to crosscheck the guy into the net? I thought it wasn’t.” On the surface, this is the normal “we say, they say” of any hockey confrontation. It’s as partisan as a mother at the principal’s office, where little Johnny can do no wrong. But this incident runs a little deeper for McDavid. And he was passionate in his post-game remarks. “Obviously, it’s a play that is a little sensitive to me. Those are plays that I’ve been really, really hurt on before,” said McDavid. “Going into the end wall, going into the net… Those type of plays I find to be dangerous. items.title: Canucks take step back in lopsided loss to Jets
items.summary: As a minimum objective, they have vowed to be competitive and difficult to play against during this rebuild. The Canucks could scarcely have been easier to beat on Thursday.
items.body: If the Vancouver Canucks weren’t already beaten when they stepped off the bus before their game in Winnipeg, they ensured themselves their 14 th loss in 15 games within the first few minutes Thursday against the Jets. items.title: Canadiens show character in comeback win over Mammoth
items.summary: Thursday’s win was the response the Canadiens were looking for after Tuesday’s embarrassing brush with history. Eric Engels explains how Montreal showed its character by coming back to beat the Mammoth in OT.
items.body: MONTREAL — This was the response the Montreal Canadiens were looking for, coming off Tuesday’s embarrassing brush with history . They choked away a four-goal lead in the final 2:39 of the third period before losing 5-4 in overtime to the Winnipeg Jets that night and wore the stench of that embarrassment for 40-odd hours before having to face off against a dynamic Utah Mammoth team Thursday. When adversity knocked early—a two-goal lead spotted to Utah on rushes gifted to Logan Cooley—the Canadiens didn’t cower; they stood up to it, firing back with two goals before the first period ended. Then they went down 3-2 and made it 3-3. And then back down 4-3 before making it 4-4. And after Cole Caufield won it in overtime—as only Caufield would, with a ripped shot over Sebastian Cossa’s shoulder—the Canadiens had confirmed what they already knew to be true about themselves. “We have a lot of character,” said Arber Xhekaj , who was one of three players to notch their first goal of the season in this 5-4 win over the Mammoth. items.title: Price took inspiration from Canadiens legends on way to Hockey Hall of Fame
items.summary: The 2026 Hockey Hall of Fame induction is Nov. 9. This year's class includes Patrice Bergeron, Cindy Curley, Carey Price, Pekka Rinne and Keith Tkachuk in the Players category, and Brian Burke in the Builders category. Here, NHL.com columnist Dave Stubbs profiles Price.
items.body: Thrived in spotlight to become winningest goalie in Montreal’s rich history The 2026 Hockey Hall of Fame induction is Nov. 9. This year's class includes Patrice Bergeron, Cindy Curley, Carey Price, Pekka Rinne and Keith Tkachuk in the Players category, and Brian Burke in the Builders category. Here, NHL.com columnist Dave Stubbs profiles Price. As he quietly slipped past Montreal Canadiens goaltending legends one after another on the all-time lists, Carey Price never more than briefly paused to consider his climb up the rankings of the NHL’s most storied franchise. On Monday, the winningest goalie on a team that’s older than the League itself will be inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame. And still, Price hasn’t sharply put into perspective his place with the Canadiens and the game at large. “I’m definitely going to be going down that road,” Price said during summertime conversation from his home in Kelowna, British Columbia. In a wide-ranging talk, Price would reflect on a remarkable body of work that brings him to Class of 2026 enshrinement in his second year of eligibility, joining many of hockey’s greatest players, brilliant goaltenders among them. Carey Price poses in the press room after winning (from left) the William M. Jennings Trophy, Vezina Trophy, Ted Lindsay Award and the Hart Memorial Trophy at the 2015 NHL Awards in Las Vegas. “When you start out, you’re not thinking that you want to be a Hall of Famer,” he said. “That’s not a goal of any kid. They just want to play hockey to the highest level they can. Honestly, I don’t think being in the Hall of Fame has hit me yet. It probably won’t until I’m sitting there in November. “When you’re in it, you’re so goal-oriented and task-focused that sometimes you lose sight of looking around and being in the present.

The significance of the moment during his National League debut became real for Jonah Neuenschwander when he heard his name announced over the public address system at Tissot Arena in Biel/Bienne, Switzerland, a place he grew up visiting as a kid. It happened when the forward, at age 15, earned the secondary assist on the opening goal for EHC Biel/Bienne in a 6-1 victory against Lausanne HC on Nov. 26, 2024, to become the youngest player in league history to get a point in his debut. "The whole evening was special for me," Neuenschwander said. "It was really cool when I found out that I would get to make my debut. Scoring a point as well made it even better. Hearing my name announced in the arena was special moment; I'll never forget that whole evening." Fast forward two seasons and it isn't surprising Neuenschwander is now one of the top Switzerland-born prospects eligible for the 2027 NHL Draft. items.title: Mintyukov, Sennecke each score twice as Ducks hand Oilers second straight loss
items.body: EDMONTON — Pavel Mintyukov and Beckett Sennecke each had two goals and an assist as the Anaheim Ducks held on for a 5-4 victory over the Edmonton Oilers on Thursday. Cutter Gauthier also scored for the Ducks (8-7-1) who have won three straight. Laurent Brossoit made 23 saves to earn the win in the Anaheim net, Evan Bouchard, Connor McDavid, Kasperi Kapanen and Leon Draisaitl responded with the goals for the Oilers (11-3-3) who have lost two in a row. Fourth-string goalie Matt Tomkins made 16 saves for Edmonton, with Tristan Jarry out due to illness and both Devon Levi and Frederik Andersen injured. The Oilers became the first team in the NHL to dress a full-time emergency backup goalie, as Brett Epp sat on the bench. Ducks: Gauthier, who came into the game with back-to-back hat tricks, extended his incredible goal-scoring streak to four games. He has nine goals, including seven on the power play during the stretch. Oilers: McDavid, who was rattled early in the game when Ducks defender Drew Helleson took him hard into the post, returned with a goal and three assists to extend his points and assist streaks to 17 games this season and give him an NHL-best 44 points. He tied for the fourth longest points streak to start a season in league history. Anaheim regained the lead 6:15 into the second period at four-on-four as Mintyukov pounced on a rebound and scored his second of the game and of the season. The Ducks power play had been unreal of late, jumping from 23.8 per cent in October to first in the NHL coming into the contest at 38 per cent. In their three previous games, they had scored on 10 of their last 12 chances. However, they went 2-for-7 against Edmonton. Oilers: Continue their homestand against the Vancouver Canucks on Saturday.

items.title: Oilers’ Podkolzin given only fighting major in scrap against Ducks
items.summary: Podkolzin was involved in an altercation with Anaheim’s Drew Helleson, but was the only one given a major penalty.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Perry Nelson-Imagn Images Remember when you were a kid, and you’d get into a fight with a sibling, but you were the one who got the harsher punishment? In the first period of a matchup between the Edmonton Oilers and Anaheim Ducks , Oilers forward Vasily Podkolzin dropped the gloves with Ducks defenseman Drew Helleson, but only one of them was handed a penalty for fighting. A little before the halfway mark of the frame, Edmonton captain Connor McDavid was driven into the Ducks’ net by Helleson, which drew the ire of the capacity crowd at Rogers Place. Podkolzin came to the aid of the best player in the world, challenging Helleson to a fight . While Helleson seemed a little hesitant to drop the gloves, Podkolzin didn’t hold his punches, giving it to the 25-year-old blueliner. However, when the penalties were dolled out, Helleson was only handed a two-minute minor for roughing. Podkolzin was given a two-minute minor for instigating a fight and a five-minute major for fighting…or as referee Cody Beach deemed it, “a one-man fight.” The 25-year-old Russian isn’t a stranger to fisticuffs . While Thursday night’s scrap was his first of the 2026-27 season, Podkolzin has been involved in 10 regular-season fights in his NHL career, also dropping the mitts late in Game 3 of last year’s Stanley Cup Playoffs, coincidentally against the Ducks , this time against Jeffrey Viel. For Helleson, it was the first fight of his NHL career, and just the second of his time in pro hockey. Back when he was with Anaheim’s American Hockey League affiliate, the San Diego Gulls, during the 2022-23 season, he exchanged blows with Matthew Stienburg, then with the Colorado Eagles.

items.summary: Cooley scored his fifth career hat trick faster than Alex Ovechkin did, doing so by two games.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Eric Bolte-Imagn Images It’s not every day that a player reaches a goal-scoring mark faster than the GR8. During a game against the Montreal Canadiens on Thursday night, Utah Mammoth forward Logan Cooley scored a hat trick, the fifth of his young NHL career. The 22-year-old accomplished the feat in just his 228th game, making him the fastest active player to register five three-goal performances. Cooley even beat the great Alex Ovechkin, as he potted his fifth hat trick two games faster than the Washington Capitals captain. Cooley found the back of the net twice before the halfway mark of the first period in the Bell Centre, giving the Mammoth an early lead. After the Canadiens came back to tie the game, the former Minnesota Golden Gopher put Utah back out in front once again just past the halfway mark of the middle frame. It was Cooley’s second hat trick in four games, as he notched a trio of goals in an overtime win against the Pittsburgh Penguins last Thursday. He added an assist in Montreal to give him a four-point night. Unfortunately for Cooley, the Canadiens got the last laugh, as Cole Caufield capped off a late comeback for the home team, scoring in overtime to give Montreal a 5-4 win. The Pittsburgh native scored his first hat trick back in his rookie season in 2023-24, when the franchise was known as the Arizona Coyotes. After not putting together a hat trick in his sophomore campaign, Cooley posted two three-goal nights last season. With his impressive outing against the Habs, Cooley now has 11 goals in the 2026-27 season, tying Toronto Maple Leafs captain Auston Matthews for fifth in the NHL in goals. But the 100-year-old World War II veteran could hardly hide his excitement about receiving that honor at Prudential Center on Thursday. The Far Hills, New Jersey native was recognized by the New Jersey Devils as part of Military Appreciation Night before their game against the St. Louis Blues. "It's a real treat, I'll tell you that," Walsh told NHL.com. "I'm going to drop the puck and that's unbelievable. I never expected anything like that." His service took him to Okinawa, Japan, where American forces began one of the Pacific campaign's bloodiest battles on April 1, 1945. Asked what inspired him to join the Marines, Walsh offered a lighthearted explanation. "I tell everybody John Wayne movies," he said with a grin. "A friend of mine joined the Marines a year ahead of me, so I thought that was pretty cool. We didn't do it together, but we ended up together, somehow." items.body: Wore lavender mullet, brought smiles to patients shooting puck from left circle ARLINGTON, Va. -- Alex Ovechkin 's office was open for visitors during the Washington Capitals' annual Hockey Fights Cancer skate at MedStar Capitals Iceplex on Thursday. Having the opportunity to shoot the puck with the NHL's all-time goal-scoring leader from his favorite spot in the left circle brought plenty of smiles from children impacted by cancer who participated in the skate with Capitals players. "To see how they smile, to see how they have fun, score goals, skate around, chat with us, it's very important and it's very cool," Ovechkin said. For the skate, each player was paired with a child from Blood Cancer United Mid-Atlantic, Make-A-Wish Mid-Atlantic, MedStar Health or Sunrise Day Camp Greater Washington. This year's skate was different, though, after Ovechkin, who holds the NHL record with 930 goals, announced Oct. 5 that this will be his final season in the League. So, instead of being paired with one child, the 41-year-old forward set up shop in the "Ovi's Office" station in the left circle, and each child took turns shooting from there. "The kids have fun," Ovechkin said. "They shoot the pucks. They (skate) around, smiling, laughing and their parents are happy, so it's very important." Ovechkin appeared to enjoy it as much as the children. Like some of them, their parents and his teammates, Ovechkin donned a lavender mullet wig to join the fun. "He's always got the biggest smile out there and has a great time," Capitals coach Spencer Carbery said. items.body: James Reimer ’s time with the New York Rangers appears to be coming to an end after making just one start that lasted one period. The Rangers put Reimer on waivers Thursday and could send him to Hartford of the American Hockey League if he is not claimed by one of the NHL’s other 31 clubs. Reimer was pulled after allowing three goals on eight shots in 20 minutes on the way to a home loss to Los Angeles on Oct. 26. New York late last month signed him to a contract for this season in the hopes that the 38-year-old could spell Dylan Garand, who had been playing almost nonstop since franchise goaltender Igor Shesterkin was lost for the season with a knee injury. Instead, Reimer struggled in his only chance, and Garand has played in 11 consecutive games. After posting a 1.85 goals-against average and .929 save percentage in his first six games, Garand is at 3.50 and .877 in his past five. Reimer going on waivers now seems to indicate Joonas Korpisalo is nearing a return from his lower-body injury. Korpisalo stopped 34 of the 37 shots he faced in a minor league rehab start with Hartford on Wednesday night. It was Korpisalo's injury during the first week of the season that set this goalie carousel in motion. The Rangers acquired him from Boston over the summer to back up Shesterkin, and Garand cleared waivers prior to opening night to go to the AHL's Wolf Pack and play regularly. Garand was recalled when Korpisalo got hurt and became the go-to option when Shesterkin went down.

If the Panthers end up bouncing back and return to Stanley Cup contention, there's a good chance he'll be a big reason why. In his initial days as an up-and-coming NHLer with the Buffalo Sabres , Sam Reinhart carried the weight of being the second-overall pick in 2014. It wasn't as if Reinhart's rookie season in Buffalo was a failure; he posted 23 goals and 42 points in 79 games, and his point total eventually grew as high as 65 points in 82 games in 2018-19. However, as the Sabres' futility to even qualify for the Stanley Cup playoffs dragged on and on, Reinhart eventually wasn't seen as part of the solution for Buffalo. So when the Sabres traded Reinhart to the Florida Panthers for goalie Devon Levi and a 2022 first-round draft pick that turned into Jiri Kulich, some Sabres fans weren't all that upset to see him go. But seeing how Reinhart has elevated his game to an elite level with the Panthers — winning two Stanley Cups and now sitting just one goal away from taking sole place of second on the franchise's all-time goal-scoring list — has to sting for Sabres fans.
